history.summary: Dedicated to a self-manifested (Swayambhu) idol of Goddess Mahalakshmi. In the early 1900s a villager named Abbayya came into possession of the idol; his home, blessed with prosperity and charity, became known as Lakshmi Nivas. His brother Thotadappa built the first shrine after the Goddess appeared in his dream asking for a temple. The temple was abandoned between 1910 and 1925; devotee Kamalamma revived worship in 1925, left after a year, and returned in 1952 to re-establish it permanently, after which it grew into a major Mahalakshmi pilgrimage site. South Indian style with a large multicoloured gopuram, set amid greenery near the Theetha Reservoir.

name: Goravanahalli Mahalakshmi Temple
town_description: Goravanahalli is a small village in Koratagere taluk of Tumkur district, near the Theetha Reservoir on the Suvarnamukhi river. Surrounded by greenery and fields, it is known almost entirely for its Mahalakshmi temple, which draws lakhs of devotees each year. (CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate — the temple is in Goravanahalli village, Koratagere Taluk, PIN 572129.)

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~100 km, verify)
travel.road: Address: Theeta Post, Koratagere Taluk, Tumkur District 572129. Accessible by road from Tumkur and Koratagere; buses and taxis available.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM–12:30 PM, 5:30–8:00 PM. Pooja 8:00–9:30 AM (Kumkuma Archana and Abhisheka); Maha Mangalarathi at 9:30 AM, 12:30 PM and 7:30 PM.
